why:
All three checks confirm the finding; I could not refute it.

(1) QUOTE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md` (3173 lines) line 2288 reads exactly: "In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), StopFailure hooks receive `error`, optional `error_details`, and optional `last_assistant_message`. The `error` field identifies the error type and is used for matcher filtering." The field table at :2292-2294 backs it (`error`, `error_details`, `last_assistant_message`), and the JSON example at :2299-2305 shows all three keys. `hooks` is row 115 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a Claude contract page, not a Codex/MCP page.

(2) CITED CODE — substance confirmed, one citation line is wrong. `packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:214-217` is exact: `case 'StopFailure': { const code = input.error_code ?? input.error ?? ''; return STOP_FAILURE_DOCUMENTED_ERROR[code] ?? code; }`, with the map at :126-142 — the matcher half is indeed fixed (commit `9a7dbf3e`, "the documented per-event matcher fields, so a matcher can fire at all"). But `pi-agent.ts:7299` is NOT the emitter: that line is a comment inside `emitStopHookOnce`. The real emitter is `emitStopFailureHookOnce` at `pi-agent.ts:7318-7324`, whose payload at :7322 is `{ hook_event_name: 'StopFailure', lifecycle_version: 1, error_code: errorCode.slice(0, 64) }` — no `error`, no `error_details`, no `last_assistant_message`. Line drift only; the claimed behaviour is confirmed 20 lines below the cite.

(3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — no upstream handler rescues it, no sibling-subsystem mix-up.
 - Layer down (what a hook actually reads): `hookCommandStdinPayload` (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-652`) is `JSON.stringify({ ...input, hook_event_name: ..., cwd: ... })` — a verbatim spread, no field renaming. Both execution authorities use it: the direct spawn (`hook-command.ts:737`) and the host's sandboxed runner (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488`, whose own comment says "One builder for both execution authorities"). So an imported Claude hook doing `input=$(cat); jq -r .error` gets null.
 - Layer up (the emit path): `emitAutomationEvent` → `dispatchAutomationAgentEvent` (`automations/lifecycle-hook-dispatcher.ts:24`) → `AutomationSystem.executeAgentEvent` (`automation-system.ts:629`) pass `input` through untouched; nothing maps `error_code` → `error`.
 - Absence checks run with `grep -a`: `error_details` has ZERO occurrences anywhere in `packages/` or `apps/` outside build `dist/` bundles — no producer, no type field (`automations/types.ts` declares `error?`, `error_code?`, `last_assistant_message?` but no `error_details`). `last_assistant_message` has a producer only for `Stop` (`pi-agent.ts:7304-7306`) and `SubagentStop`; `emitStopFailureHookOnce` takes only a code string, so the API error text available at all three call sites (`pi-agent.ts:6760`, `:6800`, `:6803`) is never forwarded.
 - Sibling-subsystem check: the one place `error` DOES arrive is the Claude-SDK backend, where the SDK itself builds the input and `buildSdkHooksForConfig` (`plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1644-1648`) spreads it verbatim — which is exactly why `getMatchValueForSdkInput` keeps the `?? input.error` fallback. That path is not ours to emit, and `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is off by default. The finding is correctly scoped to Nessy's own emitter.

The opposite is true: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md` § "Propagation found — reported, not fixed" names it twice as an OPEN item — item 2 ("`StopFailure` carries `error_code` (doc: `error`)") and item 4 ("Documented payload fields with no emitter at all: … `StopFailure`'s `error_details` and `last_assistant_message`").

NOT a deliberate product difference either: this is a hook-stdin contract key an imported Claude plugin reads, not a `NESSY_` env rename, a package-scope/binary rename, a dropped subscription flow, or gateway routing.
correctedState:
Correct as claimed, with one citation fix and one scope qualifier.

Citation fix: the emitter is `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7318-7324` (`emitStopFailureHookOnce`), payload at `:7322` — NOT `:7299`, which is a comment line inside `emitStopHookOnce`.

Corrected state: Nessy's own `StopFailure` emission carries `{ hook_event_name, lifecycle_version, error_code }` and nothing else. The MATCHER path is fixed and matches the doc (`automations/utils.ts:214-217` reads `input.error_code ?? input.error` and projects it through `STOP_FAILURE_DOCUMENTED_ERROR`, `utils.ts:126-142`; landed in `9a7dbf3e`). The PAYLOAD path is not: `hookCommandStdinPayload` (`automations/hook-command.ts:641-652`) spreads the input verbatim for both execution authorities (`hook-command.ts:737` and `server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488`), so a hook script reading the documented `.error` key gets nothing. `error_details` has zero occurrences repo-wide outside `dist/` bundles (checked with `grep -a`) — no producer and no field on `SdkAutomationInput`. `last_assistant_message` exists on the type and is produced for `Stop`/`SubagentStop` but not for `StopFailure`, even though the API error string is in hand at all three emit sites (`pi-agent.ts:6760`, `:6800`, `:6803`).

Scope qualifier the original row omits: on the Claude-SDK backend the SDK builds the hook input and `plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1644-1648` spreads it verbatim, so `error`/`error_details`/`last_assistant_message` do reach hooks there. The gap is specific to Nessy's own Pi/native emitter — which is the only `StopFailure` producer in the repo (`codex-agent.ts` and `nestor-cloud-agent.ts` emit no `StopFailure` at all, a separate and larger gap).

Status: open and already logged as such in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md` § "Propagation found — reported, not fixed", items 2 and 4.
